maya: quick sync — i'm updating the client SDK guidance for per-route rate limits. need a quick check: when a route allows a short burst (burst window) and we return a 429, should the response include both the per-route bucket header and a separate soft-burst hint?
liam: do you mean something like `x-rate-per-route-bucket` + `x-soft-burst-available`?
maya: exact. current runtime can peek ahead into pending leases and tell if a small instant burst is ok, but not sure we want to surface that in the main header contract.
serena: i'd prefer a single conservative header for backwards compat. clients that want burst visibility can opt-in via a query param or new header in the request.
jordan: what does SDK behavior look like today on 429? we return Retry-After and a JSON body with message. no extra rate headers in some flows.
maya: correct. existing 429s often only have `Retry-After`. the per-route headers were added later for quota visibility. this is about adding a second, soft-burst marker when available.
thomas: compatibility question: if we add `x-soft-burst-available: 1` on 200/429, older SDKs will ignore unknown headers. fine. risk is clients relying on only `Retry-After` semantics might mis-schedule retries if they see contradictory headers.
liam: can we sketch exact header semantics here? my proposal: 
```
x-rate-per-route-bucket: <tokens_remaining>/<reset_seconds>  # existing
x-soft-burst-available: boolean  # new, advisory only, 1/0
x-client-signal-version: 2  # indicates new advisory headers present
```
serena: +1 to versioning. if `x-client-signal-version` missing, treat `x-soft-burst-available` as not present. avoids ambiguity.
maya: good. operationally we need runtime to set soft-burst only when the lease queue is short and cacheable (no race). liam, can runtime emit this safely?
liam: yes, but with caveats: short races possible at high concurrency. we'll mark it advisory and not use it to deterministically grant tokens on client side. SDK should still obey `Retry-After` when present.
jordan: SDK change: on responses with `x-soft-burst-available=1` and status 429, SDK will schedule a micro-retry (backoff 100-250ms) before honoring `Retry-After` if request is idempotent? that seems risky.
thomas: strong +1 to not doing micro-retries automatically. better: SDK surface an opt-in config `enableSoftBurstHints` for advanced apps. default off. docs must make it clear.
maya: agreed. i'll add doc text: "advisory soft-burst hints are for observability and experiments; do not replace `Retry-After` or server-driven throttles unless developer explicitly opts-in."
liam: one more item — telemetry. runtime should emit `soft_burst_hint_emitted` metric with route and reasons (queue_length, kv_hit). will help tune.
serena: also add a lightweight smoke test: call /generate with sparse concurrency and assert that when queue<3 we sometimes see the header. this can live in the client-integration test.
jordan: pinging @ratebot for a deploy window for the header change so docs + SDK PRs align.
ratebot: build pipeline: docs PR -> canary metadata -> runtime flag -> canary deploy 0420 -> full deploy 0422. I'll create a rollout ticket. :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks — i'll open a docs PR with examples and a short SDK checklist. tagging this thread for async approvals.
liam: i'll follow up with runtime PR and add the metric. leaving a note to reviewers: watch for racey test flakes (high-concurrency CI).
thomas: i'll add the SDK opt-in flag and unit tests.
serena: created the smoke test ticket: #3456.
maya: OK all — next steps: docs PR (maya), runtime PR (liam), sdk PR (thomas), smoke test (serena). please drop quick ack here when you push.
liam: ack when I push runtime branch.
jordan: ack — i'll review the docs once maya opens it.
ratebot: ticket created: RL-2987, assigns maya/liam/thomas/serena. canary window reserved 2025-04-20 to 04-21.
maya: nice, closing the loop. :thumbsup:
